en: The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Precious Casket Seal of the Entire Body Relics of the Secret Heart of All Tathāgatas. [Translated by] Xu [Fangzhi],
Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, and Special Advancement.

The State Duke, with a fief of three thousand households, invested in purple robes, posthumously honored as Minister of Works, and bearing the posthumous title Dajian (Great Mirror), the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of the Great Guangzhi Daxingshan Temple, translated by imperial decree: Thus have I heard.
At one time, the Bhagavān was staying in the country of Magadha, at the Jewel Radiance Pond in the Stainless Garden,
together with a great assembly of bodhisattvas and a community of great śrāvakas.
He was surrounded before and behind by an immeasurable assembly of hundreds of thousands of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others.
At that time, there was a great brahmin among the assembly named Vimalaprabha (Stainless Wondrous Light),
who was learned, wise, and a joy for all to behold.
They constantly observe the ten wholesome paths of action;
they possess resolute faith and devotion toward the Triple Gem;
their virtuous mind is earnest and profound, and their wisdom is subtle and refined.
He constantly desired that all sentient beings might attain corresponding wholesome benefits,
becoming greatly wealthy, abundant, and fully endowed with all necessary provisions.
At that time, there was a brahmin named Vimalaprabha.
Rising from his seat, he went to where the Buddha was staying,
circumambulated the Buddha seven times,
and offered various fragrant flowers to the World-Honored One.
They covered the Buddha with priceless, exquisite robes, necklaces, and pearl garlands;
prostrating at his feet, they withdrew to stand to one side and made this request:
“I only pray that the World-Honored One, together with the great assembly,
will come to my residence at dawn tomorrow to accept my offerings.
At that time, the World-Honored One granted his consent by remaining silent.
At that time, the brahmin, knowing that the Buddha had accepted his invitation,
hurried back to his residence and immediately prepared a vast array of delicacies and food of a hundred flavors throughout that night.
Having erected and adorned the palace halls with various kinds of ornaments,
when morning came, he, together with his retinue,
took up many fragrant flowers and musical instruments.
Arriving at the place where the Tathāgata was, he addressed him, saying:
"The time has come; we pray that you will attend our invitation.
Now is precisely the right time."
"I pray that you will grant me your permission.
At that time, the World-Honored One, having comforted the brahmin Vimalaprabha, looked toward the great assembly and said:
"All of you should go to the home of that brahmin."
Desiring to cause them to obtain great benefit,
the World-Honored One then rose from his seat;
as soon as he had risen from his seat—
From the Buddha’s body emanate various kinds of light rays,
intermingled with wondrous colors that illuminate and touch the ten directions,
awakening all beings everywhere.
After the Tathāgata had thus awakened him,
he then set out on the road;
at that time, the brāhmaṇa, with a mind of reverence, [followed].

Carrying exquisite incense and flowers, accompanied by their retinues and the eight classes of beings— devas, nāgas, asuras, gandharvas, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, Śakra, Brahmā, and the World-Protectors—
they went before to prepare the path and escort the Tathāgata.
At that time, the World-Honored One was not far ahead on the road.
There was a garden called Abhyudgata-śrī;
within that garden stood an ancient, dilapidated stūpa,
ruined, collapsed, and overgrown with thorns.
Bramble thickets covered the ground everywhere, spreading over the gravel and pebbles so that it resembled a mound of earth.
At that time, the World-Honored One proceeded directly to the site of the stupa.
At that time, a great radiance was emitted from atop the dilapidated stupa, blazing with intense brilliance.
From within the mound of earth, a voice cried out in praise: "Excellent! Excellent! Today, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni has manifested an exceedingly sublime state."
Furthermore, he said:
"O Brahmin, you have obtained great and excellent benefit this very day."
At that time, the World-Honored One paid homage to that dilapidated stupa, circumambulated it three times to the right,
removed his upper robe to cover it,
and wept with tears streaming down his face as his snot and tears flowed together.
Having wept, he smiled.
At that moment, the Buddhas of the ten directions all gazed upon him together and likewise shed tears.
They both emitted radiance that came to illuminate this stūpa.
At that time, the great assembly gathered and all marveled at this extraordinary phenomenon.
They remained in a state of terror.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi also shed tears;
his majestic flames blazed intensely as he brandished and whirled his vajra.
He went to where the Buddha was and said to him:
"World-Honored One, for what cause and condition does this manifestation of light appear?
For what reason do tears flow thus from the Tathāgata’s eyes?"
This is the manifestation of the Buddha’s great auspicious sign of light before us.
We pray that the Tathāgata will explain my doubts to this great assembly.
At that time, the Bhagavān addressed Vajrapāṇi:
"This stūpa of the Tathāgata, which is a great mass of bodily relics,
contains the essential dhāraṇī and seal methods of all Tathāgatas, as numerous as sesame seeds."
It is now within this [stūpa].
Because Vajrapāṇi possesses this essential dharma within it,
this stūpa is itself the body of hundreds of thousands of koṭis of Tathāgatas, as numerous as sesame seeds.
It is also like a mass of the entire bodily relics of hundreds of thousands of koṭis of Tathāgatas;
even the eighty-four thousand aggregates of Dharma abide therein.
Within it is the crown-protrusion (*uṣṇīṣa*) of ninety-nine hundred thousand *koṭis* of Tathāgatas.
This stūpa has been prophesied by all the Tathāgatas.
Wherever this stūpa is located, [it shall be so].
Possessing great meritorious achievements and endowed with great majestic power, he is able to fulfill all auspicious blessings.
At that time, the great assembly, having heard this teaching of the Buddha,
became free from dust and defilement, as well as from secondary afflictions (*upakleśa*).
They attained the purity of the Dharma-eye;
among them were those who attained the fruit of Srotāpanna and those who attained the fruit of Sakṛdāgāmin.
Some attained the fruit of anāgāmin;
some attained the fruit of arhat;
and some attained the path of a pratyekabuddha.
Some entered the stage of bodhisattvas;
some attained the state of non-retrogression (avaivartika);
and some received the prediction of their future enlightenment (bodhi-vyākaraṇa).
Some attained the first bhūmi, the second bhūmi, and so on up to the tenth bhūmi;
some fulfilled the six pāramitās;
and that brahmin, far removed from dust and free from defilement, attained the five supernormal powers.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, seeing this extraordinary and rare occurrence, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, how most extraordinary and rare!
Merely hearing of this matter already yields such supreme merit."
How much more so for this essential dharma,
by planting roots of goodness within which one obtains a great mass of merit.
The Buddha said:
Listen attentively, Vajrapāṇi!
If there are sons or daughters of good family— whether bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas,
or upāsikās— who write down this sūtra.
He then transcribed the scriptures spoken by those ninety-nine hundred thousand koṭis of Tathāgatas, as numerous as sesame seeds;
that is, for those ninety-nine hundred thousand koṭis of Tathāgatas, as numerous as sesame seeds.
Having planted roots of goodness,
they are immediately protected and sustained by those Tathāgatas.
If a person reads and recites [this],...
One should then recite and chant the sūtras spoken by all the Buddhas of the past.
If one upholds this sūtra,
it is as if one were receiving from those ninety-nine hundred thousand koṭis of Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas in the ten directions— numerous as sesame seeds.
In every direction, all those Tathāgatas will provide distant protection and support, manifesting their forms day and night for anyone who makes offerings to this sutra.
Those who offer flowers, fragrant unguents, garlands, robes, and ornaments shall,
before those ninety-nine hundred thousand koṭis of Tathāgatas in the ten directions, [attain their goal].
He made offerings of divine, exquisite flowers, exquisite fragrances, garments,
and ornaments, all fashioned from the seven precious gems and piled as high as Mount Sumeru.
The planting of roots of goodness is likewise so.
At that time, the devas, nāgas, the eight classes of beings, humans, and non-humans,
having seen and heard this, each conceived a sense of wonder.
They said to one another,
"How marvelous is this majestic power!
This heap of decayed earth has been sustained by the Tathāgata’s supernormal power."
Such was this miraculous manifestation.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, by what causes and conditions [did this occur]?"
This stupa made of the seven precious jewels has now appeared as a mound of earth.
The Buddha told Vajrapāṇi:
"This is not a mound of earth; it is a great jeweled stupa formed from the seven precious jewels."
Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi, it is due to the karmic fruits of sentient beings that [the Tathāgata] remains hidden;
it is not that the complete body of the Tathāgata can be destroyed.
How could the Tathāgata’s adamantine treasury-body (vajragarbha-kāya) ever be destroyed?
It is merely because of the causes and conditions of the karmic fruits of sentient beings that [the Buddha] manifests concealment. Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi:
In the future age of the final dharma, when it is oppressed by adversity,
there will be many sentient beings who practice unrighteousness and ought to fall into hell.
Because they do not seek the Buddha, Dharma, or Saṅgha, nor plant roots of goodness,
for this reason the sublime Dharma shall go into concealment;
with the sole exception of this stūpa.
Because they are sustained by the supernatural power of all Tathāgatas,
for this reason I now shed tears;
those Tathāgatas likewise all shed tears for this same reason.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, if there is a person who transcribes this sutra and places it within a stupa, how much merit will they obtain?
The Buddha told Vajrapāṇi:
If anyone writes out this sutra and places it within a stupa,
that stupa shall become a *stūpa* of the Vajragarbha of all Tathāgatas;
it shall also become a *stūpa* empowered by the secret heart-mantra *dhāraṇī* of all Tathāgatas.
It is a stūpa for ninety-nine hundred thousand koṭis of Tathāgatas as numerous as sesame seeds;
it is also a stūpa for the Uṣṇīṣa and Locanā of all Tathāgatas.
It shall then be protected by the spiritual power of all Tathāgatas.
If it is installed within an image of the Buddha,
as well as within any stūpa, [it will be likewise protected].
For one who installs this sutra,
the image shall be made of the seven precious gems,
and the stupa shall likewise have a parasol made of the seven precious gems.
The jeweled nets and *āmalaka* finials are interlaced with the syllable *de*, and the bells are made entirely of the seven precious gems.
All Tathāgatas empower this essential Dharma with their majestic power,
sustaining it through the empowerment of their original vows and words of truth.
If there are sentient beings who are able to plant roots of goodness within this stūpa,
they will certainly attain non-retrogression from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Even those who would otherwise fall into the Avīci Hell, if they perform a single prostration and a single circumambulation of this stūpa, will certainly attain liberation;
they shall all become non-retrogressive in their progress toward Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Wherever a stūpa or an image is located,
it is protected by the spiritual power of all Tathāgatas;
that place shall not be harmed by evil winds, thunder, hail, or lightning strikes.
Furthermore, they shall not be harmed by venomous snakes, poisonous insects, or venomous beasts;
nor shall they be injured by malevolent stars, strange birds, parrots, mynas, insects, rats, tigers, wolves, bees, or scorpions.
Furthermore, there shall be no fear of yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, piśācas, or those afflicted by epilepsy;
nor shall they be afflicted by any cold or feverish diseases, scrofula, carbuncles, poisons, sores, eczema, or leprosy.
If anyone should even briefly behold this stūpa, all [afflictions] will be eliminated.
At that place, there shall be no epidemics among humans, horses, or cattle, nor among boys or girls;
furthermore, they shall not meet with untimely death.
Furthermore, they shall not be harmed by swords, staves, water,
or fire; nor shall they be invaded by enemies or oppressed by famine.
Malevolent enchantments and curses shall find no opportunity to prevail.
The Four Great Heavenly Kings, together with their retinues,
will provide protection day and night.
The twenty-eight great yakṣa generals, along with the sun,
moon, halos, comets, and the day and night deities, shall provide protection;
all the nāga kings shall infuse their vital energy to cause rain to fall in accordance with the seasons.
All the devas, along with those of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, descend three times a day;
they do so likewise for the purpose of making offerings and prostrating before the stūpa.
All the ṛṣis assemble there three times a day to offer hymns of praise and circumambulate it.
Śakra Devānām Indra, together with the celestial maidens,
descends three times each day and night to make offerings.
That place is thus protected and empowered by the mindfulness of all Tathāgatas.
If a person constructs a stūpa out of earth, stone, wood, gold, silver, or red copper,
and inscribes this essential dharma within it,
as soon as it is placed therein, that stūpa immediately becomes composed of the seven precious jewels.
The upper and lower steps, the exposed *pātra* bowls, the parasols, the bells, and the decorative nets were composed entirely of the seven precious gems.
The images of the Tathāgatas on the four sides of the stupa were likewise adorned in this same manner.
Then, sustained by the supernatural power of all Tathāgatas,
that stupa made of the seven precious jewels, which contained the great entire-body śarīras,
rose in height as far as the Akaniṣṭha heaven.
All the devas guarded and made offerings to it.
Vajrapāṇi addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, for what cause and condition does this dharma exist?"
Regarding such supreme merits,
the Buddha told Vajrapāṇi:
"By the majestic spiritual power of this Ratnakaraṇḍa-dhāraṇī..."
Vajrapāṇi said, "We pray only that the Tathāgata,
out of compassion for us, will speak this dhāraṇī."
The Buddha said:
"Listen attentively, Vajrapāṇi!
These are the bodily relics (śarīra) of all Tathāgatas—those yet to come, those of the present, and those who have already entered parinirvāṇa."
All of these are contained within the Ratnakaraṇḍa-dhāraṇī;
the three bodies (trikāya) of all Tathāgatas are likewise contained therein.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke the dhāraṇī, saying:
Namo siddhivikaraṇāya | Sarvatathāgatānām | Oṃ tribhubanavaśaṅkari vajri jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ julu julu dhara dhara | Sarvatathāgata...
8. dhātu-dhāri-patmaṃ svabhāve | 9. jayavari | 10. mukuti-samara | 11. tathāgata-dharma-cakra | 12. pramardita-nava-ḍiri ||
Bodhimanda-tri-ṅka-ra-laṃ-kṛti-sarva-tathāgata-adhiṣṭhiti-bodhaya bodhaya bodhi bodhi mucya mucya saṃ-ma.
Dhaye samavadhaya (20) tsara tsara (21) randu (22) sarvavāraṇi (23) sarvapāpaviśodhani (24) hulu hulu (25) sarvaśokamardani (26) sarva... [The text ends here.]
tathāgata hṛdaya-vajriṇi saṃbhara saṃbhara sarva-tathāgatānugrahadhāri muñca muñca svāhā.
32. *Maitre* sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhita svāhā. 33. *Dhātu-bhūte svāhā*. 34. *Samayādhiṣṭhite svāhā*. 35. *Sarvatathāgata-hṛdaya*.
Vadyatu-mudrā-svāhā (36). Subratisthitā-stambhitārhatādiṣṭe hulu hulu hūṃ hūṃ svāhā (37). Oṃ sarva... [text truncated]
Tathāgata-saṃghoṣṇīṣa-dhātu-mudrāṇi sarva-tathāgata-saṃgha-tvayi-sthiteti hūṃ hūṃ svāhā. At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this dhāraṇī.
At that time, from the site of the ruined stūpa, a stūpa made of the seven precious substances spontaneously emerged,
lofty, vast, and exquisitely adorned; it was magnificent and subtle, radiating great light.
At that time, the Tathāgatas of the ten directions— ninety-nine hundred thousand koṭis of nayutas of them—
all came to praise Śākyamuni Buddha, each speaking these words:
Excellent, excellent, Śākyamuni Tathāgata!
You are able to expound such a vast and essential Dharma and establish such a treasury of the Dharma.
In Jambudvīpa, it shall bring benefit, happiness, peace, and security to all sentient beings.
If there are sons or daughters of good family who establish this essential Dharma,
[they shall likewise attain these benefits].
For those who enshrine this dhāraṇī within stūpas or images,
we— the Buddhas of the ten directions—
will constantly follow and accompany them in whatever place they may be.
At all times, he shall empower,
protect, and mindfully guard [them] through his powers of supernormal knowledge (*abhijñā*) and the power of his vow (*praṇidhāna*).
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this Great Dhāraṇī of the Seal of the Precious Casket of the Entire Body Relics.
Having extensively performed the Buddha-work,
he then went to that brahmin’s house and accepted various offerings.
Having caused countless devas and humans to obtain great benefit and merit,

he returned to his own abode. At that time, the great assembly— consisting of bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth— [listened].
All were greatly rejoiced, believed, accepted, and practiced it.

The *Sarvatathāgata-hṛdaya-rahasya-sarvaśarīra-śarīra-ratna-peṭaka-mudrā-dhāraṇī Sūtra*. Namaḥ sarvatathāgatānām | Oṃ vajraśarīra hūṃ | Sarvatathāgata-hṛdaya-rahasya-sarvaśarīra-śarīra-ratna-peṭaka-mudrā-dhāraṇī | Svāhā.
